content.text:
**Foreign investor flows into the KOSPI** (Korea Composite Stock Price Index) have been highly volatile in 2026, with massive net selling in several months offset by strong valuation gains from the index's rally, leading to record-high foreign holdings and ownership percentages.[[1]](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20260820003100320)

### Recent Trends (2026)
- **Q2 2026**: Foreign securities investment in South Korea surged by $859.3 billion to $2.33 trillion (part of total foreign investment reaching a record $3.02 trillion, up $891.2 billion QoQ). This was driven by a 67.8% KOSPI rally in the quarter, boosting the valuation of existing holdings rather than pure inflows.[[1]](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20260820003100320)
- **May 2026**: Record net selling of ₩44.7 trillion on KOSPI (longest consecutive selling streak in years), concentrated in semiconductors like SK Hynix (₩20.7T sold) and Samsung Electronics (₩16.0T sold). Retail investors bought a record ₩35.1T to absorb some of it. Foreigners were net buyers on KOSDAQ (₩2.84T).[[2]](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/05/31/foreign-investors-dump-44-trillion-won-in-may-set-records)
- **Year-to-date through mid-2026**: Cumulative net selling exceeded ₩190 trillion on KOSPI (including alternative platforms), far above prior years, yet the index continued rising as institutions and retail stepped in. Foreign ownership still climbed due to price appreciation.[[3]](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202607092055112955)
- **June 2026**: A sharp reversal with heavy selling (e.g., ₩28T over ~8 sessions in late June/early July, including a single-day record of ₩7.73T), contributing to a steep KOSPI drop (sidecar triggered). Foreigners flipped back to net buying around July 8 as retail capitulated.[[4]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)
- **Weekly data (as of late August 2026)**: Volatile swings, e.g., net selling of ₩8.32T (Aug 24–28), buying of ₩6.55T (Aug 10–14) and ₩0.84T (Aug 17–21). Foreigners own ~30% of KOSPI market value (often ~50% in Samsung Electronics), making their flows a major driver.[[4]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)
- **Latest (as of Sep 2, 2026)**: Net selling of ₩1.92T on that day (worsening from ₩0.50T the prior day). Daily flows remain a key swing factor tied to FX, global risk appetite, and semiconductors.[[5]](https://caelion.dev/en/indicators/kospi_foreign_net_buy/)

### Broader Context
- **Ownership levels**: Foreign holdings reached record highs despite net selling in many periods, thanks to the KOSPI rally (e.g., holdings nearly doubled in some reports; ownership hit 6-year highs around 37–39% in early/mid-2026, up significantly from prior levels). US investors have been major participants.[[6]](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10677789)
- **Key drivers**: Portfolio rebalancing after big gains, semiconductor/AI exposure (heavy buying/selling in Samsung, SK Hynix), global fund flows, and FX. Foreign flows are structurally important because of their large ownership stake.[[4]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)
- **Counterparties**: Retail investors and institutions (including the National Pension Service) have often bought during foreign selling streaks, supporting the index.[[7]](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202603101813489152)

For the most granular daily or stock-level data, sources like the Korea Exchange (KRX), Naver Finance, or open datasets (e.g., GitHub repos tracking all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks) are commonly referenced.[[8]](https://github.com/james-brand/korea-market-data) Flows can shift quickly with market sentiment.
